text: The tf-idf weight of a term is the product of its term frequency in the document and its inverse document frequency, log N over df. Rare terms receive high idf.
title: TF-IDF weighting

text: BM25 ranks documents with a saturating term frequency controlled by k1 and length normalization controlled by b. It is a probabilistic retrieval function.
title: BM25

text: An inverted index maps each term to a postings list of document identifiers and term frequencies. Postings are sorted by document id to allow fast merging.
title: Inverted index

text: PageRank estimates the importance of a web page from the link graph. A random surfer follows links and teleports with a damping factor.
title: PageRank

text: Hyperlinks pointing to a page act as votes of authority. Pages linked by many important pages are considered important by the search engine.
title: Link analysis

text: Query expansion adds related terms to the user query, for example from pseudo relevance feedback on the top ranked documents, to improve recall.
title: Query expansion

text: Stemming reduces inflected words such as running and runs to a common stem run, so different word forms match. The Porter stemmer is widely used.
title: Stemming

text: Very common words like the, of and and carry little meaning and are often removed as stop words before indexing.
title: Stop words

text: Precision is the fraction of retrieved documents that are relevant and recall is the fraction of relevant documents that are retrieved. NDCG uses graded relevance.
title: Evaluation

text: Dense retrieval encodes queries and passages as vectors with a neural encoder so that semantically similar texts are close in the embedding space.
title: Dense retrieval

text: A lock provides mutual exclusion so that only one thread enters the critical section at a time, preventing a race condition on shared data.
title: Mutual exclusion

text: A semaphore is an integer with sem_wait and sem_post operations. A binary semaphore can be used as a lock to protect shared information.
title: Semaphores

text: Deadlock occurs when two threads each hold a lock and wait forever for the lock held by the other. Lock ordering prevents circular wait.
title: Deadlock

text: Virtual memory gives each process the illusion of a large private address space. The hardware translates virtual addresses to physical addresses.
title: Virtual memory

text: A translation lookaside buffer caches recent virtual to physical page translations to speed up address translation. A TLB miss walks the page table.
title: TLB

text: The multi-level feedback queue scheduler uses several priority queues and moves jobs between them based on observed behaviour, boosting priority to avoid starvation.
title: Scheduling

text: Journaling file systems write intended updates to a write-ahead log before applying them, so the file system can recover consistency after a crash.
title: Journaling

text: TCP Reno uses slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit and fast recovery to adapt the sending rate when the network is congested.
title: TCP congestion control

text: The address resolution protocol maps an IP address to a hardware Ethernet address on the local network using a broadcast request.
title: ARP

text: 802.11 wireless LANs use CSMA/CA, carrier sense multiple access with collision avoidance, because collisions cannot be detected while transmitting.
title: Wireless

text: Two-phase locking has a growing phase where locks are acquired and a shrinking phase where they are released, guaranteeing conflict serializable schedules.
title: Two-phase locking

text: The ARIES recovery algorithm uses write-ahead logging, analysis, redo and undo phases so that committed transactions survive a crash.
title: Recovery

text: Dijkstra's algorithm computes shortest paths from a source with non-negative edge weights; Bellman-Ford also handles negative edges.
title: Shortest paths

text: A Bloom filter answers set membership queries with a small bit array and several hash functions, allowing false positives but no false negatives.
title: Bloom filter

text: Kruskal's algorithm builds a minimum spanning tree by adding the cheapest edge that does not create a cycle, using a union-find structure.
title: Minimum spanning tree

text: Dynamic programming solves problems with overlapping subproblems by memoizing the answers to subproblems in a table.
title: Dynamic programming
